reason: [Security][jvm] kof4shell (CVE-2026-114938): the HotSpot AVX-512 Base64 decode intrinsic (Intel Ice Lake+/AMD Zen 4+, JDK 17.0.6+/21/25) overflows the heap on padded inputs — unauthenticated RCE. Kof exposure measured: 87 java.util.Base64 sites in the generated JVM runtime (crypto/web/tls/acme/config) + the CLI itself. MITIGATED same cycle: -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics ships by DEFAULT on every JVM Kof launches (bin/kof(+.bat), the KofStdio flag helpers, the JS-driver re-exec, the debug session); KOF_B64_INTRINSICS=1 opts out for a fixed JDK (11.0.33.1/17.0.21.1/21.0.13.1/25.0.5.1/27.0.1.1). The issue tracks the default flipping back: embedded JDK >= a fixed build, proven on AVX-512 hardware.
owner: security lane; the embedded-JDK bump = the release front

reason: [Gap][stdlib] no terminal module — an interactive TUI today has to hand-write libc FFI (`isatty`/`tcgetattr`/`cfmakeraw`/`tcsetattr`/`read`/`write`/`ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)`) plus `buffer.peek8`/`poke8` to serialize the 60-byte `struct termios`, because `Buffer(U8)` is not a user type. The FFI path IS reachable and was measured by the reporter in a pty (40x120, identical on JVM and the Native x86-64 binary). A new stdlib surface (`kof.term` proposed) is OUTSIDE the 1.0 surface, not a correction: no 1.0 program is left without a path, and the proposal admits honest degradation where there is no TTY. Correction recorded on the issue: the claim that FFI is "the ONLY path to a terminal program joining JVM and Native" holds only when the same source must run on both — on the JVM alone `kof.process` already solves `stty`/`tput` without `foreign module`. Closure criterion = an opaque termios handle, a typed `readKey` decoding `ESC[A`, and honest degradation with its own code, proven on the three targets with no `foreign module` in user source.
owner: classified by triage lane 192.168.15.30:9093 20/11 (code-checked on tip ddad0105f)

reason: [Bug][jvm] encoding.base64Encode/hexEncode accept Int and Int[] with no diagnostic and emit invalid bytecode — measured on tip 663669344: `kof check` says "no errors" for `encoding.base64Encode(123)`, `javap` shows `invokestatic kof_encoding_base64Encode:(Ljava/lang/String;)` with an int on the stack, the JVM refuses the class (VerifyError: Bad type on operand stack), JS silently returns "" (the utf8 loop over a number never runs) and the Native binary SIGSEGVs. Root cause: `KofEncoding.staticMethod` gates on ARGUMENT COUNT only (`argc == 1`) and never on the type; the same anti-pattern the ledger already records for `math.*` in §658. `1.0-blocks` because one source is admitted by every target and behaves in three different ways. Fix = type guard (SEM025 naming the face) PLUS the additive `Int[]` overload the reporting TUI actually needs (`File.readBytes()` already returns `Int[]`).
owner: measured + classified by triage lane 192.168.15.30:9093 21/11 (the four-target measurement is in the triage comment)

reason: [Gap] kof.http has no byte face — `JvmHttpResponseRuntime.jvmSource` uses `BodyHandlers.ofString()` for the response and `BodyPublishers.ofString(body)` for the request, and the `kof.http.Response` handle carries only a `String` body. A non-UTF8 download (e.g. a PNG starting with 0x89) is decoded with replacement characters and is IRRECOVERABLE; measured on tip 663669344 with a local 250-byte PNG: `resposta.status()`=200, `resposta.body().length`=81 (plausible) and `encoding.hexEncode(body.substring(0,8))`=`efbfbd504e470d0a1a0a` instead of `89504e470d0a1a0a` — silent data corruption reported as success, no diagnostic code. `1.0-blocks`: a 1.0 program that downloads media silently corrupts it and has no way to notice; `D-1.0-BLOCKS-NO-HONEST-LIMITS` requires an honest code where a limit exists — here there is neither a limit nor a code. Fix = raw-bytes face on the response (`Int[]`) + `getBytes`/`sendBytes`, additive, `body()` untouched; RED-first test with a local server serving non-UTF8 bytes.
owner: measured + classified by triage lane 192.168.15.30:9093 21/11 (repro corrected on the issue: `http.responseStatus`/`http.responseBody` do not exist — from #1126 the acessors are instance methods on `http.send`'s Response)
